title: God's About to Drop the Hammer
paragraphs: § God Takes the Witness Stand
This is the message God gave to Micah from Moresheth. It happened back when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah. It was all about the drama going down in Samaria and Jerusalem.
Listen up, everyone! Earth, you and everyone on it, pay attention: The Lord GOD is about to testify against you, coming straight from His holy temple.

Look, here He comes! God is on the move from His place! He's striding across the highest mountains. The mountains are literally melting under His feet, and the valleys are splitting wide open, like wax in a fire or water rushing downhill. This is all happening because of Jacob's screw-up, because the house of Israel messed up. You ask what Jacob's big sin is? Just look at Samaria—isn't it obvious? And all those sex-and-religion shrines in Judah—isn't Jerusalem responsible?

“So I'm about to turn Samaria into a heap of rubble, a vacant lot littered with garbage. I'll dump the stones from her buildings into the valley and leave her abandoned foundations exposed. All her carved and cast gods and goddesses will be sold for stove wood and scrap metal. All her sacred fertility groves burned to the ground. All the sticks and stones she worshiped as gods, destroyed. These were her earnings from her life as a prostitute. This is what happens to a prostitute's fees.”

Because of this, I'm going to weep and wail. I'll go around barefoot and stripped of my clothes. I'll howl like a jackal and moan like an owl. Her wound is incurable; it has spread all the way to Judah. It has reached the gate of my people, all the way to Jerusalem itself.

Don't gossip about this in Telltown. Don't even waste your tears. In Dustville, go roll around in the dust. In Alarmtown, the alarm is going off. The people of Exitburgh are never getting out alive. Mourn for Last-Stand City—there's nothing left standing there. The villagers of Bittertown keep waiting for something sweet, but harsh judgment from God has marched right into Peace City. All you folks in Chariotville, hitch up your chariots and run! You got the daughter of Zion hooked on trusting chariots instead of God. Israel's sins got their start with you too. Go ahead and hand your goodbye gifts to Good-byeville. Miragetown promised a lot but left Israel's kings disappointed. Inheritance City has lost its inheritance. Glorytown has seen its last bit of glory. Shave your heads in mourning for your precious kids. Go bald as a goose egg—they're being dragged into exile and they're not coming back.

title: God's Plan vs. Theirs: It's Over
paragraphs: § God Has Had Enough

It's so over for you guys who lie in bed dreaming up ways to do people wrong. First thing in the morning, you're up and at 'em, using all your energy to make it happen. You see a field you like, you just grab it. You find a house you want, you just take it. You bully a guy and his whole family, only seeing people for what you can get from them. But God is so done. He's like, "I've got some plans of my own, and it's a disaster with your name on it because of all this evil you're into. You're all on the chopping block now. There's no getting away from this one. It's your doomsday." People are gonna make up roast tracks about you, and you'll be the ones singing the blues: 'We're totally wrecked, our homes and lands are being auctioned off. They're taking everything and leaving us with nothing! It's all going to the highest bidder.' And when that happens, there will be no one to have your back, no one to speak up for you when you're facing God's judgment.

"Stop preaching," the preachers are saying. "Don't preach all that negative stuff. Nothing bad is gonna happen to us. Why are you talking like this to Jacob's family? Does God just lose his temper? Is this really how He acts? Isn't He on the side of good people? Doesn't He help those who hustle?"

"'Good people'? Seriously? You're the real enemy of my people! You jump people who are just out for a chill evening walk. You literally take the coats off their backs like you're looting in a war zone. You force the women of my people out of their own nice homes. You turn their kids into victims, leaving them exposed to all kinds of messed-up stuff. Get out of here, all of you. This isn't your chill spot anymore! You've contaminated this place, and now you're contaminated—totally ruined! But hey, if some guy showed up with a charming smile and a smooth tongue, lying 24/7 like, 'I'll preach you a sermon on how to get anything you want from God: more cash, the best wine... you name it'—you'd make him your personal preacher on the spot.

"But I'm calling a meeting, Jacob. I want everyone back—every last survivor of Israel. I'm gonna gather them all in one place, like a whole flock of sheep in a pen, like cattle in a corral—a massive crowd of people heading home! Then I, God, will bust open all the gates and lead them out into freedom. They'll follow their King. And I'll be right there at the front, leading the way."

title: God vs. Corrupt Leaders: It's a Showdown
paragraphs: § Haters of Good, Lovers of Evil
Then I said:

“Alright, listen up, you so-called leaders of Jacob and Israel. Do you even know what justice is? Seriously? You guys hate what's good and love what's evil. Isn't justice, like, your main job? But instead, you're skinning my people alive, ripping the meat right off their bones. You break their bones, chop them up, and throw them in a pot like you're making some kind of messed-up stew.
But a time is coming when you'll be crying out to God for help, and He's gonna leave you on read. He's gonna turn His back on you because of all the messed-up stuff you've done.

And here's God's message to the prophets who are straight-up lying to my people: As long as they're getting paid and eating good, they're all like, 'Life is amazing! Peace and love, everyone!' But the second you stop paying them or disagree with them, their 'God bless' turns into 'God curse you' real quick. So, guess what? You're going blind. You won't see a thing. You'll be living in the shadows, completely clueless. The sun is setting on you prophets. Your time in the spotlight is over. From now on, it's all darkness. The visionaries will be confused, and the experts will be all mixed up. They'll hide behind their reputations and make lame excuses for not knowing God.
But me? I'm filled with God's power. I've got His Spirit of justice and strength, and I'm ready to call out Jacob for their crimes and Israel for their sin.

You leaders of Jacob and Israel are a piece of work. You laugh at justice and twist the truth. You're building up your precious city, Zion, on the backs of the people you've killed, and expanding Jerusalem with your crimes. The judges are taking bribes, the priests are selling their teachings like merch, and the prophets are preaching for cash. And all the while, you're pretending to be tight with God, saying, 'We've got God on our side. He'll protect us.' Because of people like you, Zion will be turned back into a farm, Jerusalem will become a pile of rubble, and instead of the Temple on the mountain, there will just be a bunch of scraggly trees.

title: The Ultimate Comeback Story
paragraphs: § The Making of God’s People

But look, when it all goes down, God's Temple on the mountain is gonna be the main attraction, towering over everything else. People from all over will be flooding in, and nations will be like, 'Yo, let's go up to God's mountain, to the Temple of the God of Jacob. He'll show us how to really live.' The realest teaching is gonna come from Zion, God's truth straight from Jerusalem. He's gonna sort out all the drama between nations and settle fights from far away. They'll trade their weapons for garden tools—swords into shovels, spears into rakes. Nations will stop fighting and forget how to go to war. Everyone will just be chilling in their own backyard, safe and sound. The Commander of Heaven's Armies said it, and He's not kidding.
Meanwhile, everyone else is just doing whatever, picking their own gods. But us? We're sticking with our God, staying loyal forever.

'On that day,' God says, 'I'm gonna gather up everyone who's been hurt and kicked out, all the ones I had to discipline. I'll take the broken ones and make them an elite crew. The ones who were lost will become a super strong nation—a living showcase of what God's rule looks like. And I'll be ruling from Mount Zion, from now until forever.'
And you guys, the stragglers of Jerusalem, just trying to get by in your run-down neighborhoods: the old glory is coming back. Jerusalem is gonna be the center of the kingdom again.

So why are you all freaking out? Don't you have a king? Is he slacking off or something, making you panic like a woman in labor? Well, go on, scream and cry, Daughter Jerusalem. It's gonna feel like childbirth. You'll be kicked out of the city, forced to camp out in the open. Then you'll end up in Babylon. But here's the plot twist: what you lose in Jerusalem, you'll get back in Babylon. God will rescue you and give you a fresh start, right from under your enemies' noses.

But for now, a bunch of godless nations are teaming up against you. They're saying, 'Let's take her down while she's weak! Let's see Zion get humiliated.' These haters have no clue what God is actually up to. They don't realize He's forging His people, like separating wheat from the chaff, or refining gold.

So get up, Daughter of Zion! It's time to get refined. I'm making you an unstoppable force, God's own wrecking ball to smash these godless nations. You'll bring all their stolen goods back as a holy offering to God, all their wealth to the Master of the whole earth.

title: The Small-Town King with the Ultimate Glow-Up
paragraphs: § The Leader Who Will Shepherd-Rule Israel
But for now, brace yourselves, Jerusalem. It's about to get rough. The enemy has you surrounded, and they're going to totally humiliate Israel's king, slapping him around like a rag doll.

But yo, listen up. Bethlehem, from David's old stomping grounds—you might be considered a nobody, the runt of the litter. But out of you is gonna come the leader who will shepherd Israel. And this ain't some random new guy or pretender; his family tree is ancient and distinguished. Meanwhile, Israel will be in foster homes until the birth pangs are over and the child is born, and the scattered brothers come back home to the family of Israel. He'll stand strong, leading with God's power, shining with the majesty of God's name. And everyone will be safe and sound, because the whole world will see how great he is—the ultimate Peacemaker.

And if some bully nation like Assyria tries to invade our land, don't even sweat it. We'll put him in his place, send him packing, and watch his every move. Shepherd-rule will stretch as far as needed, to Assyria and all the other Nimrod-bullies. Our shepherd-ruler will be our hero, saving us from any enemy, old or new, who tries to mess with our home.

The purged and select crew from Jacob's family will be like an island in a sea of peoples. They'll be like dew from God, like rain showers that just show up without being on the weather app—totally unplanned and out of human control.

Yeah, this purged and select crew from Jacob will be like an island in a sea of peoples—like the king of beasts among wild animals, like a young lion loose in a flock of sheep, killing and devouring the lambs, and no one can stop him. With your arms raised in triumph over your enemies, they'll be gone for good!

"God says, 'A day is coming when I'm getting rid of all your weapons of war. For real. I'll destroy your war horses and your chariots. I'll tear down your military bases and flatten your forts. I'll get rid of all your fake religion and your dark magic stuff. I'm gonna smash all your idols and sacred poles you've been worshiping. You're done trying to control everything and worshiping the stuff you make. I'll rip out all your corrupt centers of power and destroy anyone who defies me. With some serious anger, I'm gonna wipe out all the godless nations that refused to listen.'"

title: God's Got a Complaint... And He's Not Holding Back
paragraphs: § What God Is Looking For
Alright, listen up, God's laying it all out.

"Get ready for court. If you've got a beef, tell it to the mountains; make your case to the hills. And now, you mountains, listen to God's case; you, Earth's jury, pay attention—'cause I'm bringing charges against my own people. I'm building a case against Israel."

"My people, how have I wronged you? Have I been a burden, worn you out? Seriously, tell me! I'm the one who got you out of that terrible life in Egypt; I paid a high price to free you from slavery. I sent Moses to lead you—and Aaron and Miriam too! Don't you remember what King Balak of Moab tried to pull, and how Balaam son of Beor flipped the script on him? Remember all those stories from Shittim to Gilgal. You gotta keep all of God's salvation stories fresh in your mind."

So, how do I even show up before God and give Him the respect He deserves? Should I roll up with a ton of offerings, like some prime year-old calves? Would God be impressed with thousands of rams, or like, rivers of olive oil? Would He be moved if I sacrificed my firstborn, my own precious kid, just to cancel out my sin?

But for real, He's already made it super clear how to live, what to do, and what He's looking for. It's actually pretty simple: Do what's right and fair to others, be compassionate and loyal in your love, and don't take yourself too seriously—take God seriously.
Yo, pay attention! God's calling out the city! If you know what's good for you, you'll listen. So listen up, everyone! This is major.

"You really expect me to ignore the disgusting amount of money you've made by cheating and being fake? You think I'm cool with your shady deals and sneaky plans? I'm so over the rich and powerful bullying their way through life with bluffs and lies. I'm done. Starting now, it's over for you. You'll pay for your sins, every last bit. No matter how much you get, it'll never be enough—you'll always feel empty inside. No matter how hard you grind, you'll have nothing to show for it—just a bankrupt life and a wasted soul. You'll plant grass but never get a lawn. You'll make jelly but never get to taste it. You'll press apples but never drink the cider. You've been living by the messed-up standards of King Omri and the trashy lifestyle of Ahab's family. Since you've been blindly following their trends, I'm about to make you bankrupt. Your whole way of life will become a joke, something people laugh at. Your lives will be seen as pointless and fake."

title: Down But Not Out: The Ultimate Comeback Story
paragraphs: § Stick Around to See What God Will Do

Man, I'm just so over it, totally bummed out. It's like going to the garden to pick cabbages, carrots, and corn, and coming back empty-handed—nothing for soup, sandwich, or salad. There's literally not one good person left. It feels like decent people have gone extinct. Everyone's just out for themselves, preying on each other like animals.

They've all mastered the art of being terrible. Corrupt leaders are always looking for a handout, and the super-rich make sure they always get their way. The people who seem the best are actually the most toxic, and the so-called top-tier are just trash. But that's all about to end. It's judgment time. Just watch them all get exposed and shamed. Don't trust your neighbor, don't even tell your secrets to your best friend. You gotta watch what you say, even with your own spouse. Whole neighborhoods and families are just falling apart. The closer people are to you—your own kids, your in-laws—the worse it can get. Your own family can turn into your biggest enemy.
But me? I'm not giving up. I'm sticking around to see what God's gonna do. I'm waiting for God to come through and make things right. I'm counting on Him to hear me out.
§ Spreading Your Wings

So, to my enemies, don't celebrate just yet. I might be down, but I'm definitely not out. Yeah, I'm sitting in the dark right now, but God is my light. I can handle God being angry with me. I messed up, I sinned, so I deserve it. But I know it won't last forever. He's on my team and He's going to get me out of this mess. He'll flip the switch and show me His plan. I'll finally see the big picture and how He was right all along. And my enemies will see it too and be totally humiliated—yeah, disgraced. The same enemies who kept mocking me, asking, 'So where's this God of yours now?' I'm gonna see them get taken down like trash in the street with my own two eyes.

Oh, that's gonna be a legendary day! A day to rebuild your city, a day to finally stretch your wings and be free. All your people who were scattered everywhere will come back home, old friends and family from all over the world, from Assyria in the east to Egypt in the west, from across the oceans and over the mountains. But for everyone else, it's gonna be the opposite—a total ghost town—all because of how they chose to live and the messed-up things they did.

God, please lead your people with your shepherd's staff, your precious flock that belongs only to you. Let them graze in lush Bashan, just like in the good old days in green Gilead. Bring back the same insane miracles you did when we escaped from Egypt. And as for the nations that don't follow you? Put them in their place. Humble them, shut them up, and leave them clueless. Make them crawl away like snakes and bugs, coming out of their hiding spots to face our God. Make them tremble with a holy fear.

Where is another god who even compares to you? You wipe our slate clean of all guilt, choosing to ignore the past sins of your precious people. You don't hold on to your anger forever, because showing mercy is your thing. That's what you love to do most. And I know your compassion is coming for us. You'll crush all our wrongdoing. You'll throw our sins into the deepest part of the ocean. You'll keep your promise to our ancestor Jacob and continue to show the same love you showed to Abraham—everything you promised our ancestors a long, long time ago.
